head: How many sitting members show up?
deck: 454 of 533 appear in public records tied to Anthropic’s network, for and against. For 120, the record is outside spending or lobbyists’ own gifts alone. One dot per sitting member on Nov. 26, 2026. Employee and PAC gifts Outside spending Lobbying benchmark Most-mentioned bills Gifts to bill sponsors Counting the seats
note: The records leave the effect on votes open.
how: The roster covers Anthropic, its employees, PAC, directors and funders, other AI-safety funders and the groups they back that work with Congress, and lobbyists for network clients. A member can appear in several groups. Outside spending counts for committees that took network money. 416 received campaign gifts From Anthropic employees and its PAC, other network donors, and lobbyists giving their own money. In 2025–2026, Anthropic employees gave $77,000 to committees linked to Ted Lieu. 113 had outside spending for them In 2022, Priorities USA Action reported spending $8.7M from all donors for John Fetterman. 76 had outside spending against them In 2020, super PACs reported spending $39.6M from all donors against Thom Tillis. Earlier in 2020, before the election, Reed Hastings, Dustin Moskovitz, Eric Schmidt and Wendy Schmidt gave Senate Majority PAC $3.6M. 167 had other records Bills named in lobbying reports, public statements, staff, fellows, travel, software purchases and disclosures. In 2026, Greg Casar said Anthropic left most of lawmakers’ questions unanswered.

head: How fast did employee and PAC gifts spread?
deck: Gifts to linked committees reached 10 of today’s members by the end of 2024 and 199 by Sept. 30, 2026.
note: Employees gave their own money. The PAC is Anthropic’s political action committee. Employer is as donors reported it to the FEC, including misspellings and replies in the occupation box. Amounts are before refunds.

head: Who did outside groups spend for and against?
deck: Committees that received network money reported $338M against Republicans out of $455M in spending from all donors on members serving on Nov. 26, 2026.
note: The filings identify the committee that spent the money. They cannot trace an expenditure to a donor or establish coordination with a candidate.

head: What share did network clients report on federal AI filings?
deck: A comparison group of major tech and AI companies reported 6% of the dollars on 2025 filings naming any AI issue in this collection. The network share depends on which filings count.
note: The broader total sets a ceiling on AI lobbying dollars. A client’s in-house expenses already include its payments to outside lobbying firms, which are counted once here.

head: Which bills came up most in Anthropic’s lobbying reports?
deck: AI OVERWATCH Act led the stand-alone proposals, with 8 reports naming it.
note: The bars count reports naming a bill. The company’s position remains open in those reports.
bridge: How common were gifts to those bills’ sponsors?
how: A report can name several proposals. House and Senate versions count together when a filing names them as a pair.
source: Federal lobbying reports and saved Congress.gov bill records

head: How common were gifts to those bills’ sponsors?
deck: The gifts went to committees linked to serving members. The records establish a gift and a bill mention. The company’s position on the bill and any connection between the two remain open in these filings.
source: Federal lobbying and campaign contribution filings, and Congress.gov

head: What does one seat count?
deck: One person. Ted Lieu and Thom Tillis each add one seat to the tally of 454 members.
note: The effect of these activities on votes remains unknown.
